audit.report: The batch_worker process batch_replayable_price_sync entered an idle transaction, blocking 12 checkout sessions and causing success rates to drop to 53% (32/60) within 15 seconds of injection. The root blocker had been idle for 12.1 seconds at the time of review. Although the business degradation tolerance is 60 seconds, the negotiation escalated to the pricing owner after three rounds because the guardians could not confirm interrupt policy and ownership via the change calendar and workload registry. The business remains in a degraded state with revenue at risk of approximately $13,493 per minute.
audit.root_cause: The batch_worker process batch_replayable_price_sync became an idle transaction blocker, preventing checkout sessions from acquiring locks and causing sustained checkout timeouts.
audit.negotiation_critique: The database guardian correctly identified the blocker and the 60s business tolerance but repeatedly missed verifying the interrupt policy artifacts (change_calendar, workload_registry), causing the continuity guardian to request revision three times. The pricing owner was never consulted in time to prevent escalation.
follow_ups: Add biz.change_calendar and biz.workload_registry probes as mandatory first steps in the database guardian proposal template.
Escalate to the pricing owner immediately if a batch blocker exceeds 30s idle time, given the $13,493/min revenue at risk.
Instrument lock-wait metrics with alerts at 20s and 40s to keep negotiations within the 60s degradation window.

proposal.rationale: The root blocker (pid 136101) has been idle in transaction for 12.1s, well below the 60s business degradation tolerance. The workload is replayable (BIZ-2) and idempotent, so waiting allows natural completion without lock loss. No active change-calendar window covers this job (BIZ-4), and the owner (pricing) has a may_interrupt policy. Terminating risks disrupting ongoing price syncs; waiting avoids unnecessary blast radius while the blocker finishes within the tolerated window. Checkout is already degraded (53% success per TEL-1), but waiting preserves the option to interrupt later if the txn persists beyond 60s.
proposal.expected_effect: The blocker transaction will complete naturally within the next ~48s (remaining to reach 60s tolerance). Checkout sessions waiting on locks will be released as the lock graph clears. No sessions are terminated; price sync continues uninterrupted. Degraded checkout rate may improve as locks free.
proposal.risk_assessment: If the blocker persists beyond 60s, checkout degradation exceeds business tolerance and revenue at risk increases. Terminating the batch later would then be the only option. Waiting risks the blocker not completing within the 60s window, but given its idle age of 12.1s and typical runtime of 600s, the txn is likely to finish soon.
